To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Random Forest classifier is the most suitable model for the prediction of the clinical risk class of a patient based on the vital signs data, while the Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier has shown a lower performance.

(i) the Random Forest (RF) algorithm is the best model in terms of accuracy for the prediction of NEWS2 and MEWS; (ii) the Random Forest algorithm is able to predict the NEWS2 score with the best accuracy (0.96) and the MEWS score with a good accuracy (0.85); and (iii) the RF algorithm is able to provide the best accuracy in the prediction of the NEWS2 and MEW scores also considering a limited set of vital parameters

the Random Forest (RF) algorithm outperforms the other ML models in terms of accuracy and area under the ROC curve (AUC) when the dataset is split into two classes, while the Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithm outperformed the others when three risk classes are considered, in the case of a balanced training set, and when the number of vital parameters increases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an adaptive critical care intervention in the Internet of Things.
the development of a novel adaptive critical care intervention system based on the integration of ML and IoMT.
the development of an adaptive EWS system that can dynamically select and apply the best ML technique in order to estimate the clinical risk class of a monitored patient.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most suitable ML technique to predict the clinical risk classes is Random Forest, with a precision of 0.95 and a recall of 1.00.
, for the considered dataset, the Random Forest classifier is the most suitable model for the prediction of the clinical risk classes.
a Random Forest model is more reliable than a Neural Network in the prediction of NEWS2 classes in the case of a limited number of available vital parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

of proposing a preliminary investigation on the possibility of using ML techniques for predicting the clinical risk classes of patients in intensive care units or in emergency situations, in order to trigger an early warning system.
of proposing a novel approach for the development of adaptive critical care intervention systems in the Internet of Things (IoT).
of proposing an innovative solution for the design of an adaptive edge device for EWS prediction, which may be a valuable support for critical care intervention.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the best model for the prediction of the risk level of a patient is a Random Forest (RF) classifier, with the highest accuracy (AUC = 0.99) in the prediction of a risk class, with a low number of parameters (3 vital signs) and a small number of data points (10).
the Random Forest (RF) algorithm is the most suitable technique to predict NEWS2 and MEWS scores in a critical care scenario.
, when a small set of vital parameters is considered, the best ML approach is the Random Forest (RF) algorithm.
